description: Consensus proposals and validations received from peers, and transaction relay efficiency for this node.

panels.title: Peer Proposal Receive Rate
panels.description:
**What:** How many consensus proposals this node receives from peers per second.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of received proposals over 5 minutes, per node.
**Reading it:** A steady rate roughly proportional to the number of proposing validators.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; scales with validator count and connectivity.
**Watch for:** A drop toward zero (isolation from the network) or a sudden flood far above baseline (proposal spam).
**Source:** src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp:PeerImp::onMessage(TMProposeSet)

panels.title: Peer Validation Receive Rate
panels.description:
**What:** How many ledger validations this node receives from peers per second.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of received validations over 5 minutes, per node.
**Reading it:** Steady and proportional to the number of validators the node hears from.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; roughly one burst per validator per closed ledger.
**Watch for:** A fall toward zero (loss of validator connectivity) or an abnormal surge from untrusted sources.
**Source:** src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp:PeerImp::onMessage(TMValidation)

panels.title: Proposals Trusted vs Untrusted
panels.description:
**What:** The share of received proposals that come from trusted (UNL) validators versus everyone else.
**How it's computed:** Received-proposal rate split by trust status over 5 minutes, shown as proportions.
**Reading it:** A healthy node with a good UNL shows a solid trusted slice.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; a meaningful trusted fraction is expected.
**Watch for:** A collapsing trusted share or a large untrusted volume, consistent with proposal flooding from non-UNL peers.
**Source:** src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp:PeerImp::onMessage(TMProposeSet)

targets.expr: sum by (proposal_trusted, exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", proposal_trusted=~"$proposal_trusted", span_name="peer.proposal.receive"}[5m]))

panels.title: Validations Trusted vs Untrusted
panels.description:
**What:** The share of received validations from trusted (UNL) validators versus untrusted sources.
**How it's computed:** Received-validation rate split by trust status over 5 minutes, shown as proportions.
**Reading it:** The trusted slice should dominate for a well-configured node.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; trusted validations expected to be the majority.
**Watch for:** A shrinking trusted share or a spike of untrusted validations, which can indicate misconfiguration or abuse.
**Source:** src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp:PeerImp::onMessage(TMValidation)

panels.title: Reduce-Relay Peer Selection
panels.description:
**What:** How transaction relay picks peers: chosen relay sources, suppressed peers, and peers with the feature off.
**How it's computed:** Current peer counts in each category (selected, suppressed, not-enabled), per node.
**Reading it:** A high suppressed-to-selected ratio means relay is saving bandwidth as intended.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; suppressed should exceed selected in a well-connected mesh.
**Watch for:** A large not-enabled count (older peers forcing full relay) or selected climbing while suppressed falls.
**Source:** src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp:registerReduceRelayGauge

panels.title: Reduce-Relay Missing-Tx Frequency
panels.description:
**What:** How often a peer has to fetch a transaction it missed because relay suppressed it.
**How it's computed:** The reported frequency of on-demand missing-transaction fetches, per node.
**Reading it:** Lower is better; near-flat means suppression is well tuned.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; a low, stable value is expected.
**Watch for:** A rising trend, meaning suppression is too aggressive and the on-demand fetch path is growing.
**Source:** src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp:registerReduceRelayGauge
